_note: Where the hero and each companion stand after the written story's choices (scene flags the chapter decisions do not cover). Each entry is told to the AI game master (src/director.js prompt: hero.standing, party[].standing) and shown in the Journal when its `when` holds, checked like a written line's when (src/expansion.js lineApplies). Facts only: what was chosen, never what to do with it.

entries.text: The hero's Second Oath answers to the council of the free wards, which can recall them by two-thirds.
The hero's Second Oath answers to Briarwatch, the town that took them in.
The hero's Second Oath answers to the people they walk with: their companions.
The hero's Second Oath answers to no one: to what is right, as best they can see it.
Nessa wrote Wren a long yes: she will take Cinder Fold's forge-signal after her, but not yet.
Nessa is keeper of Cinder Fold's forge-signal. Wren gave her the key at the pit before she was cast into the tenth bell.
Nessa turned her long yes into a real one: she went back over the pass in the spring to take the forge-signal from Wren.
Nessa's yes to Wren's post is held for her. Wren keeps the forge-signal from a chair, alive and still angry about it.
Nessa turned down Wren's forge-signal post in a letter she sealed herself, and chose the road with the hero. Wren kept the no and will not ask again.
Wren was cast into Cinder Fold's tenth bell. The miners' committee holds the signal key Nessa said no to.
Nessa never answered Wren's offer of the forge-signal. The letter is still in her pocket.
Hal's company, the forty Orin once failed to come back for on the south road, took the council's service.
Hal's company, the forty Orin once failed to come back for on the south road, stayed with the guild.
At the Mother Bell, Hal held the iron doors so Orin didn't have to. Somebody else held the door.
At the Mother Bell, Orin held the iron doors the first night, and the second time he did not have to.
At Vell the hero argued that Orin be tried with his old captain Varn for leaving Saltwick. Mags Peller forgave him, and he went to keep Saltwick's lamps for a spring.
At Vell the hero argued that Orin be tried with his old captain Varn for leaving Saltwick. Mags Peller would not forgive him: it was the fourteen's to forgive, not hers.
At Vell the hero argued that Orin be tried with his old captain Varn for leaving Saltwick, and given the same.
At Vell the hero argued that Captain Varn alone be tried for Saltwick, not Orin, who only followed the order.
At Vell nobody was judged for Saltwick: Varn was sent back to Hesk with a message.
In the deep, Orin gave up the Saltwick night. He no longer remembers it, and knows that he did.
Maren let her list of lost shrine keepers go in Merrowgate harbour. Her new list is the people of the Sallows long room, each with something true beside them.
Maren still keeps her list of lost shrine keepers, with one empty space and Elske Marrow's name below it, nothing written beside it yet.
Maren is the free wards' seal: every week at Highpass she sits across from people who have come to give, and hears them.
In the deep, Maren gave up the day her gift woke. She has forgotten it, and knows she has.
Maren keeps no list now. She goes to the shrine on the Briarwood side in the mornings, and sits, and comes back.
In the deep, Nessa gave up one thing she remembered about Wren, and does not know which.
The hero told Elske Marrow what they saw in Hollin's Reach, and that its bell had stopped.
The hero never told Elske Marrow what they saw in Hollin's Reach. It was hers to tell.
